title: Computerized radix sorting
summary: Harold Seward's memory-efficient method made digit-by-digit sorting practical on computers.

parents.reason: Hollerith-style digit passes on punched cards supplied the sorting method Seward adapted for computer memory.

title: Shellsort
summary: Donald Shell's gap-based insertion passes moved distant out-of-order elements before a final ordinary insertion pass.

title: Symmetric binary B-tree
summary: Rudolf Bayer's order-four B-tree form represented balanced multiway search paths in a binary structure.

parents.reason: Bayer's symmetric binary form was explicitly a special order-four case of the B-tree structure.

title: Red–black tree
summary: Color invariants encoded balanced multiway search trees as binary trees with bounded path lengths.

parents.reason: Guibas and Sedgewick derived the red–black representation from Bayer's symmetric binary B-tree.

title: Leaf-oriented B+ tree indexing
summary: By 1973, B+ tree indexing in VSAM kept records in linked leaves to reduce block reads.

parents.reason: The B+ tree is a B-tree variant retaining high-fanout indexing while placing records in leaves.
File blocks were the physical pages B+ trees were designed to index: high-fanout internal nodes locate records stored in leaf pages.
parents.directContribution: Block storage shaped the B+ tree's structure: high-fanout internal nodes reduce page reads, while record values stay in linked leaf pages for indexed retrieval.

title: Trie string search
summary: Character-by-character paths indexed variable-length keys by their shared prefixes.

title: Bloom filter
summary: A compact probabilistic membership test avoids many unnecessary exact lookups.

parents.reason: Bloom proposed a much smaller probabilistic alternative where conventional error-free hash tables consumed too much memory.

title: Linear hashing
summary: Incremental bucket splitting let hash files grow without periodically rebuilding the entire index.

parents.reason: Linear hashing extends hash-table lookup to growing files by splitting one bucket at a time as records accumulate.

title: IBM Information Management System
summary: IMS deployed a hierarchical database and transaction system for engineering and Apollo parts records.

parents.reason: The initial DATE system used the recently introduced hard disk to query part numbers and revision relationships across terminals.

title: IBM System R
summary: IBM began System R research in 1974 to implement relational databases and demonstrate transaction performance.

parents.reason: System R was built to implement Codd's relational database ideas as a working system with demonstrated transaction performance.

title: Ingres relational database research system
summary: Berkeley published its Ingres relational database research papers in 1973, exploring a DBMS with QUEL.

parents.reason: Berkeley researchers began the project after reading papers on relational databases and pursued a separate research implementation.

title: Oracle Database
summary: Oracle brought an early SQL relational database to commercial release.

parents.reason: Oracle's first commercial release implemented the relational database model as a general-purpose database product.
parents.directContribution: The relational model independently supplies Oracle's table, row, key, and relationship structure; SQL supplies the separate query language used to operate on it.

parents.reason: The 1979 Oracle release was among the earliest commercially available database systems to use SQL.

title: Second and third normal forms
summary: Codd's later normal forms constrained relation dependencies to reduce insertion, update, and deletion anomalies.

parents.reason: Codd defined second and third normal forms as dependency rules for organizing relations in the relational database model.

title: Entity–relationship model
summary: Peter Chen's diagrams represented entities and their relationships before mapping them into database schemas.

title: Data warehouse
summary: In 1988, Devlin and Murphy described an architecture integrating operational data for decision support.

parents.reason: Warehousing drew together data held in operational databases and separated analytic access from transaction workloads.

title: Express OLAP system
summary: Released in 1970, Express was the first product to perform online analytical processing queries.

title: Introsort
summary: A depth-limited quicksort falls back to heapsort to bound worst-case running time.

parents.reason: Musser's hybrid begins with quicksort to retain its fast average performance on typical data.
Introsort switches to heapsort when recursion grows too deep, bounding the worst-case sort time.

title: Timsort
summary: A stable hybrid sort detects existing ordered runs and merges them efficiently.

parents.reason: Timsort was derived from merge sort, using run merging as its main operation on ordered subsequences.
